newsitem.title: ITALY: Six institutions show interest in Banco Napoli.
newsitem.headline: Six institutions show interest in Banco Napoli.

text.p: Three Italian and three foreign institutions are interested in the sale of a 60 percent stake in struggling Banco di Napoli which is on the block as part of a plan to salvage the loss-making bank.
Southern Italy's largest bank is temporarily under the control of the Italian Treasury after piling up a record loss of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.1 billion) last year.
Under pressure from the European Commission to sell the ailing bank by the end of the year, the Treasury gave companies until November 18 to express an initial interest in the sale.

"A total of six financial institutions, three Italian and three international, have declared an interest in participating in the sale process of Banco di Napoli," a statement from the bank said on Tuesday.
They now have until December 20 to make a full bid.

Banco di Napoli said the highest bidder would take the stake, adding that it would not reveal the names of the companies and groups which had expressed an interest in order to ensure the maximum competitivity in the sale process.
Italy's Treasury-controlled Banca Nazionale di Lavoro (BNL) and recently-privatised insurer INA announced on Monday they had shown preliminary joint interest.

But besides them, no other group has stepped forward publically and Britain's NatWest, Germany's Bayerische Landesbank and the Netherlands' Rabobank all denied Italian press reports that they might be considering separate bids.

Companies which have expressed interest now have the right to study information being prepared on Banco di Napoli by merchant bank N.M. Rothschild, which has been retained by the Treasury as an advisor.
After last year's losses, the southern bank plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year thanks largely to a poor, highly politicised loan policy.
The Treasury, stepping into the breach, has installed new management and promises to take on the bulk of the company's stock of bad debt before it sells the problematic bank.
